newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Columbia CEO sees no slowdown.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Columbia CEO sees no slowdown.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp sees no signs of a slowdown in business due to the sweeping government investigations that have engulfed the company in recent days, said chief executive Dr. Thomas Frist on Tuesday.
"This company is still exceeding overall industry trends relative to others," Frist said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
Asked if the probes into the company's activities have damaged the business, Frist said, "We haven't seen that."
He said the company's own polls of patient, employee and physician satisfaction have not shown any negative trends.
Columbia, the largest U.S. for-profit hospital company, is scheduled to report second-quarter results on Wednesday.
The Nashville, Tenn.-based firm is expected to report earnings of $0.62 per share, up from $0.54 per share a year ago, according to the First Call consensus.
Frist declined to comment on other telltale indicators of the company's growth momentum, such as growth in same-hospital revenues and same-hospital admissions.
Historically, Columbia has been able to grow same-hospital admission more than two percent annually and same-hospital revenues by more than seven percent annually.
The industry average for same-hospital revenue growth is about five percent, analysts said.
Shares in Columbia closed up 1/16 at 34-3/8 Tuesday on the New York Stock Exchange on heavy trading volume.
